reviews.title: Paywalls basic functions
reviews.text:
The app is set up where you can do most of the basic functions without paying including swiping through profiles, setting up your own profile, and access to a calendar of events close by. 

However they don’t tell you until you’ve matched with someone that you have to subscribe in order to connect with them. This is the main purpose of the app and I didn’t know that I had to pay the subscription just to see and connect with who matched with me. 

If you’re willing to pay the subscription for an occasional match it works and you’re going to need it if you want to actually connect with them.

reviews.title: Info about boosting
reviews.text:
I’ve been on the fence about paying for this app, it seems that they’ve recently made it so that you only can match if you pay for premium, so I decided to pay 8$ to boost my profile for one day, here’s what I learned:

My profile was shown to 204 people. Out of those 204 only 2 people liked my profile. Apparently my profile is only shown to 0.2 people every day, because in the boost report it says that 204 people is 1000% more people than normal. I received one match, who immediately unmatched with me.

The bottom line is that if you don’t pay for premium you will NEVER match with anyone.

reviews.title: Steep price
reviews.text:
Mutual used to be a dating app with a decent value, but unfortunately its pricing has followed the same trend as many other dating apps. What once felt reasonably priced is now up to around $60 per month, which is pretty hard to justify for a dating app.

What makes it even more frustrating is how the matching system seems to work. If someone has already liked you, it often feels like the algorithm removes or limits the chances of that person naturally appearing in your regular swiping options. That means you may never come across someone who already expressed interest in you unless you pay for the subscription that lets you see who liked you.

It creates the impression that potential matches are being placed behind a paywall instead of allowing people to naturally connect through normal swiping. I like the concept behind Mutual and the community it serves, but the increasing price and the way likes are handled make the app feel much more focused on getting users to subscribe than actually helping people connect.

reviews.title: A basic waste of time…. And money
reviews.text:
There have been recent updates to this app that make it less and less appealing to use. It has basically become a pay to play app (I’ve paid before, and had worse results). 

I can swipe through hundreds of profiles and not come across anyone who has “liked” me (and I’ve done this multiple times, most recently counted as I viewed 200 profiles, liked a few of them, but none of them were people who liked me as evidenced by the number of likes not going down like it used to). This tells me that the only way you’re now going to see a profile of someone who liked you is if you pay to see it. 

I get more “likes” on the free membership than I have when I’ve paid, which also makes me believe that the likes I am seeing are bots (which also would explain why when you match with someone who liked your profile on the same day, there aren’t any responses), and simply bait to get you to buy a membership.

There are way better apps out there, free or paid, that produce better results of connections. Sure they aren’t members of the church (but I’ve connected with quite a few non members using this app), but they are local and you have a much larger dating pool to choose from.

I like that Mutual’s an app for members to connect but it’s just horribly managed and they keep removing features rather than adding them. 

I regret having ever spent money on subscriptions (I’ve spent $60 total) and never will waste my money here again, perhaps if they reimplement or improve the free features I’d be more willing to pay money to the developers in return.

reviews.title: Not very many attractive people on here. Don’t waste your time or money. Keep your distance
reviews.text:
I swipe up probably less than 1% of the time. I’ll spend 45 minutes of my free time just swiping down. Takes FOREVER to come across someone that’s decent looking. Paid for one month. No more. I’ll literally swipe down through all of the available choices for my age group and the only way to get more options is if I extend the age down to 13 years younger than me. Nothing here. Huge waste of time and money. Spend that $20 per month where they are more options. Definitely not here.

One possibility is that there is an algorithm that sees who turns you down and then categorizes you based on the opinion of a few ladies, which would be extremely stupid. (Make it so that you only see Butch or unattractive ladies). You know, get rejected by a few women that never get rejected and then get thrown into the bone pile to mingle with the grub. Not all women think the same or are attracted to the same type of look. I’ve been rejected by hot women and I’ve had hot women enthusiastically go on dates with me. Different strokes for different folks. Case in point: have you ever seen a beautiful lady dating a guy and think “How did he get HER?” It happens. Categorizing someone based on the taste of a few ladies is horribly simple and gives a terrible experience to willing subscribers. Maybe they’re afraid of men harassing women? Which seems almost impossible to do on the app.

If I’m wrong and I’m truly seeing all the choices, it’s only a matter of time for this app.
